questions.q: What does Tableau's own "form follows function" principle mean for chart selection?
options: The visualization you build should be driven by the question you're asking and your data's properties, not chosen first and justified afterward
Every chart type must use the same color palette for consistency
Form and function are unrelated concerns in Tableau
Charts should always default to whatever Show Me suggests first
questions.explain: Tableau's documentation frames chart choice as depending on the question being asked and the data's properties — the visualization serves the analysis, not the other way around.

questions.q: Which analytical category does a scatter plot with a trend line primarily answer, per Tableau's framework?
options: Correlation — whether two measures are related, and how strongly
Spatial — geographic patterns in the data
Ranking — the relative rank of dimension members
Change over time — how a measure has shifted across dates
questions.explain: Scatter plots (with optional trend lines) are Tableau's primary tool for the Correlation category — examining whether and how strongly two measures relate.

questions.q: Why can the same chart type, like a bar chart, appear under more than one analytical category (magnitude, deviation, ranking)?
options: Because the chart type alone doesn't determine the question — what's on the axis and how it's sorted or compared determines which question it's actually answering
Because Tableau randomly assigns categories to chart types
Because bar charts are the only chart type capable of appearing in multiple categories
Because magnitude, deviation, and ranking are actually the same category with different names
questions.explain: A bar chart can show magnitude, deviation from a baseline, or ranking depending entirely on framing and setup — the chart type itself never tells you the question, your framing does.

questions.q: According to the three-question process in this lesson, what should you determine BEFORE opening Show Me?
options: The actual question you're trying to answer, which analytical category it falls under, and which chart type in that category fits your available dimensions and measures
Which color palette looks best with your company branding
How many total rows exist in the connected data source
Whether the data source is a live connection or an extract
questions.explain: The lesson's process is to identify the real question first, map it to a category, then pick the fitting chart type — using Show Me only afterward, to build the chart already decided on.

questions.q: What is the risk of opening Show Me before answering the three-question process?
options: It only shows what's technically possible given your current fields, not which chart type actually answers your real question
Show Me will refuse to open until the three questions are answered
It will permanently delete any dimensions not used in the chosen chart
There is no risk — Show Me always identifies the correct chart automatically
questions.explain: Show Me evaluates field requirements, not intent — used first, it can only suggest what your current fields technically support, not the chart that truly fits your analytical question.
